html:
Bábism was a messianic religious movement begun in Iran in 1844 by a young merchant of Shiraz, Sayyid Ali Muhammad, who took the title the Báb, meaning "the Gate".

Shia Muslims awaited the return of the hidden twelfth Imam. The Báb claimed first to be the gate to him, then to be the promised one himself, and he announced a new revelation that replaced Islamic law. His message spread fast among clerics, merchants and villagers.

The Qajar state and the Shia clergy saw it as heresy and revolt. Bábis fought armed risings in several towns, and the Báb was shot by firing squad in Tabriz in 1850. After a failed attempt on the shah's life in 1852, thousands of followers were killed.

Most surviving Bábis later followed Baháʼu'lláh, who said he was the one the Báb had foretold. Out of this came the Baháʼí Faith.
sum: Bábism was a messianic religious movement begun in Iran in 1844 by a young merchant of Shiraz, Sayyid Ali Muhammad, who took the title the Báb, meaning "the Gate".
